research_concepts: adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix
methodological_questions: Does adherence to the recommended mix predict series winning after controlling for team talent?
How is adherence measured, and is it independent of the outcome it is meant to predict?
Is the number of series (54 in the task; 55 in FAM:SF-APPS-030 and FAM:SF-APPS-027) enough to detect a plausible effect?
Do the 2025-26 playoff series have final outcomes on the question date (2026-06-16)?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether teams that ran BEST counters more and AVOID less after suppression win more series, on 55 series (110 series-directions). Spearman BEST vs won rho=+0.131 p=0.1723; AVOID vs won rho=-0.098 p=0.3099. Verdict recorded as null. INSUFF_EVIDENCE was 91.5% of triggers. Mean PPP BEST 1.395 vs AVOID 0.865.

Series-level AVOID share vs winning. Game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008, flagged as inflated by n and team-quality confounding. Series-level rho=-0.26 p=0.07 with n=50, described as underpowered (about 80 series needed for p<0.05). Verdict inconclusive.

Adaptation quality (pct_ran_BEST minus pct_ran_AVOID) vs series wins with RS net-rating talent control, n=55 series. Talent per-series logistic p=0.0213; adaptation p=0.2755 after talent control. Team-in-series cluster: talent p=0.0095, adaptation p=0.2449. corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124.

Pivoting to a listed counter after suppression sustains higher PPP than not pivoting. 10/12 pairs CONSISTENT and within 0.10 of non-pivot, with no PIVOT_WINS. Two pairs with enough signal were PIVOT_LOSES (PNR->PULL_UP 1.069 vs 1.224, n=9; DRIVE->PULL_UP 1.101 vs 1.217, n=5). Failure mechanism recorded as adequately powered null, n=74 matchups.

Pregame predicted series winner matched 27 CONFIRMED / 18 CONTRADICTED of 45 (60%), with no CI reported. Canonical-10 team-side Spearman median about 0.536. Per-series Spearmans range from -0.024 to 0.905. Recorded as a hand-maintained headline file.

Three-level counter ranking (population, team, matchup). The best counter after DRIVE was CUT in L1 but PNR in L2 for MIA, so the L1 and L2 rankings disagree. Playoff n_matchups ranged from 4 to 44. No validation recorded.

Sequential conditioning premiums (CUT->PULL_UP +0.065, PUTBACK->TRANSITION +0.084). A DRIVE->PNR premium of +0.326 was later removed as 'doesn't hold up'. Reason not stated in the files read. Verdict abandoned.

Season stability of top suppressors: only 2/30 stars (7%) met the 75% same-top-suppressor rule across 4 seasons. Some negative teammate sequential pairs reported (e.g. Tatum->Porzingis DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.444, n=31). Failure mechanism recorded as adequately powered null.

Star suppression by lineup and forced play type (Jokic, Curry, Doncic, Giannis) with PPP gaps of about -0.36 to -0.54 in cells of n=30 to 59. No placebo or matching. Later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

Defensive PPP allowed and possession share, RS vs playoffs, for 25 teams. DRIVE allowed PPP fell 1.191 to 0.923. PNR share rose +12.1pp, which may reflect tagging differences. Descriptive only, no inferential test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing BEST/AVOID run-rate alignment as a predictor of series wins across 55 series
failed_approaches.why: Alignment-win Spearmans not significant (p=0.172 and 0.310). Recorded as A_unanswerable with 91.5% of triggers at INSUFF_EVIDENCE, meaning the sample could not support the test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level AVOID share as a predictor of losing, separated from team quality
failed_approaches.why: Underpowered at n=50 (p=0.07). Game-level significance was inflated by n. Still confounded by team quality, recorded as A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Adaptation quality as a predictor of series wins after talent control
failed_approaches.why: Adaptation p=0.275 after talent control. Talent is correlated with adaptation (+0.124), and n~55 cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality. Recorded as A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pivoting to a listed counter after suppression as a sustained PPP advantage
failed_approaches.why: Adequately powered null (B_powered_null). Most deltas were under 0.10, and two pairs showed pivot worse than staying.
Only 2/30 stars met the stability rule. Adequately powered null (B_powered_null).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Specific sequence premiums (for example CUT->PULL_UP, PUTBACK->TRANSITION)
failed_approaches.why: Premium later removed as 'doesn't hold up'. Reason not stated in the files read (E_unclear). Recorded as abandoned.

evidence_establishes: Series-level tests of coaching adherence or counter alignment against wins, using about 50 to 55 series in this project, have been null or inconclusive (FAM:SF-APPS-030, FAM:SF-APPS-027, FAM:SF-CHT-039).
Team talent is a strong predictor of series wins in the same data, and it is correlated with adaptation, so it must be controlled (FAM:SF-APPS-027, where talent per-series logistic p=0.0213).
Within-series PPP-level pivot and counter effects were small and mostly not significant in the matchups that were tested (FAM:SF-APPM-054).
Star-level suppressor identities were not stable across seasons (FAM:SF-APPA-058), and earlier star-chain gaps were treated as artifacts without placebo checks (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence to the recommended mix predicts winning under a pre-registered definition of adherence, since no retrieved record tests that exact definition with a pre-specified threshold.
Whether a larger sample (roughly 80 or more series, as FAM:SF-CHT-039 estimates) would show an effect, because the retrieved records give no power calculation for the adherence measure.
Whether 2025-26 playoff series are usable at the question date. The retrieved records do not cover this season's status.
The effect of tagging or measurement error on the adherence classification. FAM:SF-APPS-012 notes possible tagging differences but does not quantify them.
own_inferences: The question as posed is close to FAM:SF-APPS-030 and FAM:SF-APPS-027. Both were run on about 55 series and returned null or untestable. A near-identical test on 54 series is unlikely to change the picture without a different design.

Adherence is probably defined from the same play-by-play used for PPP, so a team that wins also tends to have higher PPP and better suppression numbers. This makes the adherence measure partly outcome-derived.
Talent is the most likely confounder. Teams with good rosters both win series and adapt more, so a raw association would mostly reflect roster quality.

Using a series-level outcome with 54 units leaves very little power. Any defensible test would need either a far larger sample (game or possession level with clustering) or a narrow pre-specified hypothesis.
The history of nulls and inconclusive results suggests that the counter-mix framing has been tested repeatedly without a stable signal.
uncertainties: The unit count is 54 series in the task statement but 55 in FAM:SF-APPS-030 and FAM:SF-APPS-027. The reason for the difference is not given in the records.
The 2025-26 playoff data is partial on 2026-06-16 and complete only from 2026-06-21. Series outcomes for that season are not final on the question date.
The exact definition of 'suppression-conditional recommended mix' and of 'adherence' is not stated in the task or the retrieved records.
The retrieved records do not show whether any earlier test used pre-registration, held-out seasons, or placebo outcomes.
FAM:SF-APPM-033 gives no sample size or reason for removal, so its premium findings cannot be relied on in either direction.
FAM:SF-APPS-056 reports a 60% winner hit rate with no confidence interval, so it cannot be distinguished from chance (50%) with the information given.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval showed that the closest earlier tests (FAM:SF-APPS-030, FAM:SF-APPS-027, FAM:SF-CHT-039) were run on similar series counts and returned null or untestable results, with talent confounding recorded. This lowers the likelihood that a series-level adherence test with 54 units will produce a usable result, so the decision moved from a standard proceed toward do_not_proceed. The retrieved evidence does not show that the question is impossible, so a minimum viable test is still described below.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series is far below the roughly 80 series that FAM:SF-CHT-039 estimated for p<0.05 at the observed effect, and earlier series-level tests on about 55 series were null or underpowered.
Team talent drives both winning and adaptation (corr +0.124 in FAM:SF-APPS-027). Series-level adherence cannot be separated from roster quality with this sample.
Adherence classes (BEST/AVOID/PIVOT) are derived from PPP computed from the same play-by-play that defines winning, so the predictor and outcome are not independent.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work in this project tested closely related questions (counter alignment and adaptation vs series wins, AVOID share vs losing) on about 50 to 55 series. All returned null, underpowered, or untestable results, and talent confounding was recorded. The retrieved records do not test a pre-specified adherence threshold, so the exact question is only partly answered.

risks.text: About 54 series gives very limited power. Earlier series-level tests with 50 to 55 series were underpowered (FAM:SF-CHT-039, FAM:SF-APPS-030).
Team talent confounds adherence and winning. The talent-adjusted adaptation effect was p=0.275 (FAM:SF-APPS-027).
Adherence is defined from PPP that also depends on the outcome, so the adherence-winning association may be partly mechanical.

Using full 2025-26 playoff data, which is only complete from 2026-06-21, would leak future outcomes into a question dated 2026-06-16. Any 2025-26 playoff series must be excluded or its status verified before use.
Play-type tagging may differ across seasons and source feeds. FAM:SF-APPS-012 reports a +12.1pp PNR share jump that may reflect tagging differences.
Many play types, counters, and pair-level comparisons have been screened across the project (FAM:SF-APPM-054, FAM:SF-APPM-055). Without correction, a single significant result could be spurious.
FAM:SF-CHT-009 reported star-chain PPP gaps without placebo or matching, and later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.
Low-volume play-type cells (n=5 to 9 matchups in FAM:SF-APPM-054 and FAM:SF-APPM-055) have PPP estimates driven by small-sample noise and possession floors.

Seasons 2022-23 through 2025-26 may differ in rules, pace, and play-type tagging. FAM:SF-APPM-033 premiums were removed and FAM:SF-APPS-056 is a hand-maintained headline file, so stability across seasons is not established.
A coin-flip baseline gives 50% series winner accuracy. FAM:SF-APPS-056 reports 60% (27/45) with no CI, which is not clearly above chance with this sample.

design.estimand: Association between a pre-registered adherence score (share of triggered possessions where the team ran the recommended counter) and series win, adjusted for pre-season team talent (RS net rating) and a placebo outcome. This is a minimum viable test, not a claim that the current framing is sound.
design.unit: Team-series (two per series), with possession-level adherence aggregated to the series. Analysis is clustered by team and season.
design.sample: Series in 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 playoffs only (completed seasons). 2025-26 playoff series are excluded until final outcomes are verified. Reconcile the 54 vs 55 series count against the source before analysis.
design.power: Before analysis, run a power calculation for the target effect. The records suggest roughly 80 or more series are needed for p<0.05 at the effect size seen in FAM:SF-CHT-039. If the available sample cannot reach that, report the test as underpowered and do not claim a null.
design.controls: Adjust for RS net rating, playoff seeding, and opponent talent. Use a talent-matched comparison or a residualised adherence measure. Use a placebo outcome (for example, a non-series game outcome or a pre-series prediction) and a held-out season. Fix the play-type tagging version across seasons.
design.falsification: The hypothesis is falsified if the talent-adjusted adherence coefficient is not positive with a CI excluding a pre-specified minimum effect, or if the placebo outcome shows a similar association. A placebo association would indicate artifact or confounding.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary test (adherence to the recommended mix vs winning). Treat all other counters, play types and pair analyses as exploratory, with Holm or FDR correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the pre-registered adherence coefficient, adjusted for talent, is positive with a 95% CI excluding zero, survives the placebo check, and holds on the held-out season. Otherwise report as null or untestable. Do not proceed to a causal claim.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, with the 2025-26 playoffs excluded (partial on 2026-06-16, complete only from 2026-06-21). The 2025-26 regular season may be used for talent only if complete on the analysis date (complete from 2026-04-13). Record file hashes and tagging version.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series winning?
How should adherence be measured and validated across 54 series?
What confounders and leakage risks threaten a test of adherence versus winning?
args.query: suppression-conditional recommended defensive mix adherence predicts winning series NBA playoffs 2022-23 through 2025-26

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
